blocks.text: The median is the middle value of a dataset arranged in order. If the number of values is odd it is the middle value; if even, it is the average of the two middle values. In biology it represents the centre better than the mean for things like population size, disease prevalence or body measurements, where the data may not be normally distributed. There is no single formula, only steps.

items: Arrange the data in ascending or descending order.
Count the number of values, n.
If n is odd, the median is the value at position (n + 1) / 2.
If n is even, the median is the average of the values at positions n / 2 and n / 2 + 1.

blocks.text: Odd number: plant heights 50, 65, 60, 75 and 80 cm. Ordered: 50, 60, 65, 75, 80; n = 5; the median is the 3rd value, 65 cm. Even number: animal weights 300, 400, 330, 315, 450 and 500 kg. Ordered: 300, 315, 330, 400, 450, 500; n = 6; the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th values, (330 + 400) / 2 = 365 kg.

blocks.prompt: The heights of six children are 110, 115, 118, 120, 122 and 125 cm. What is the median?
blocks.explanation: n = 6 is even, so the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th values: (118 + 120) / 2 = 119 cm.

items: Order the data; odd n: middle value; even n: average of the two middle values.
